title: Vegan Orange Cream Cupcakes
shortDescription: Soft vegan orange cupcakes with fresh zest, topped with a creamsicle vanilla swirl. Prep takes 25 minutes, bake takes 18.
description: These cupcakes taste like a creamsicle in cake form. I tested this batch three times in my own kitchen to get the orange flavor bright, not soapy. Fresh zest goes right into the batter and the frosting, so every bite tastes like real orange, not fake candy flavor. The crumb stays soft and moist thanks to plant milk and oil instead of butter and eggs The frosting is a simple vegan buttercream with vanilla and a little more zest swirled through. It pipes tall and holds its shape at room temperature for a few hours. This is a good one for spring parties or anyone missing that orange push-up pop from childhood. It is fully vegan, so it works for mixed dessert tables without any substitutions needed.
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F. Line a 12-cup muffin pan with paper liners.
Whisk flour, baking powder, baking soda, and salt in a large bowl.
In a second bowl, mix orange juice, plant milk, oil, vanilla, vinegar, and orange zest.
Pour the wet mix into the dry mix. Stir until just combined, no dry streaks.
Divide batter evenly among liners, filling each about two thirds full.
Bake 16 to 18 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean. Cool in the pan 5 minutes, then move to a rack.
Let cupcakes cool fully before frosting, about 45 minutes.
Beat vegan butter until smooth. Add powdered sugar one cup at a time, beating between additions.
Mix in orange zest, plant milk, and vanilla. Beat 2 more minutes until light and fluffy.
Pipe frosting high in a swirl using a large star tip. Add extra zest on top if you like.
tips: Zest your orange before you juice it. It is much harder to zest a juiced orange.
Use room temperature vegan butter for frosting, straight from the fridge it will not whip smooth.
If your batter looks slightly curdled from the citrus, that is normal. It bakes up fine.
Store frosted cupcakes in the fridge, but let them sit out 20 minutes before serving for best texture.

faq.question: Can I use bottled orange juice instead of fresh?
faq.answer: Fresh juice works much better here. Bottled juice is often more acidic and less sweet, which can throw off the batter's balance and flatten the orange flavor.

faq.question: Why does my frosting taste bitter?
faq.answer: This usually means too much white pith got into the zest. Zest only the bright orange outer layer and stop once you hit the white part.

faq.question: Can I make these gluten-free?
faq.answer: Yes, swap in a 1:1 gluten-free flour blend. The texture will be slightly denser but the orange flavor stays the same.

faq.question: How do I get the creamsicle color without dye?
faq.answer: A tiny pinch of turmeric gives a natural warm yellow-orange tint to the frosting. Start with just a pinch, it colors fast.

conclusion: These orange cream cupcakes are an easy way to bring creamsicle flavor to a vegan dessert table. The zest keeps things bright and the swirl frosting makes them look bakery-made with very little effort.
